quests.instruction: The wings of this insect are covered in thousands of tiny scales that make colourful patterns. Which insect?
quests.hint: Touch one gently and some powdery dust may come off on your finger.
quests.explanation: A butterfly's wings are covered with tiny overlapping scales. They give the wings their colours.
quests.funFact: Butterflies and moths belong to a group whose name means "scale wing".
quests.question: Butterfly

quests.instruction: What flying animal has wings made of thin skin stretched between very long finger bones?
quests.hint: Look inside its wing and you'll find bones laid out like a hand.
quests.explanation: A bat's wing is a flexible sheet of skin held by long finger bones, so it can twist and turn sharply in the air.
quests.funFact: Bats can swerve in mid-air to snatch a flying insect.
quests.question: Bat

quests.instruction: Which bird rides rising columns of warm air, circling higher without flapping its wings?
quests.hint: It saves energy by letting the air do the lifting.
quests.explanation: Broad wings let an eagle soar. Warm air rising from the ground, called a thermal, lifts it up with hardly any effort.
quests.funFact: Some big eagles can soar for hours with hardly a wingbeat.
quests.question: Eagle

quests.instruction: Pick the swimmer that pushes through the water by moving its tail up and down instead of side to side.
quests.hint: Its backbone bends like a runner's, up and down.
quests.explanation: Whales and dolphins swish their tail flukes up and down. Fish swing their tails from side to side.
quests.funFact: Scientists can tell individual humpback whales apart by the pattern on the underside of their tails.
quests.question: Whale

quests.instruction: Which reptile has flippers instead of feet for flying through the sea?
quests.hint: Its front limbs paddle like wings.
quests.explanation: Sea turtles have paddle-shaped flippers. The front ones push them forward and the back ones help steer.
quests.funFact: Leatherback turtles can dive deeper than 1,000 metres.
quests.question: Turtle

quests.instruction: Name the animal that uses gills to breathe and fins to steer.
quests.hint: Both parts are made for living fully underwater.
quests.explanation: Gills take oxygen from the water, and fins help the fish steer, balance and stop.
quests.funFact: Many fish have a gas-filled bag inside called a swim bladder that helps them float at the right depth.
quests.question: Fish

quests.instruction: Spot the sea-shore animal that wears its skeleton on the outside, like a suit of armour.
quests.hint: It has to shed its armour whenever it grows too big for it.
quests.explanation: A crab's hard shell is an outside skeleton called an exoskeleton. It protects the soft body underneath.
quests.funFact: Crabs breathe with gills, and those gills must stay damp, even for crabs that spend time on land.
quests.question: Crab

quests.instruction: Which animal's shell grows in a spiral, with new coils added as it gets bigger?
quests.hint: The shell grows in a coil, not in flat plates.
quests.explanation: A snail's shell is made by its own body. As the snail grows, it adds more material to the open edge, making the spiral bigger.
quests.funFact: In dry weather a snail can seal the opening of its shell with dried slime to stop itself drying out.
quests.question: Snail

quests.instruction: This spotted insect lifts its hard, shiny cover before it flies. Which insect?
quests.hint: Underneath the cover are thin wings for flying.
quests.explanation: A ladybug's hard front wings are covers that protect the delicate flying wings beneath. They lift up before it takes off.
quests.funFact: The number of spots on a ladybug depends on its kind, not its age.
quests.question: Ladybug

quests.instruction: Find the giant that uses its long ivory tusks to dig for water and strip bark off trees.
quests.hint: Its tusks are really enormous front teeth.
quests.explanation: An elephant's tusks are long front teeth. It uses them for digging, lifting and stripping bark.
quests.funFact: Elephants can be right-tusked or left-tusked, a little like people are right- or left-handed.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Pick the animal that grows bony branches on its head and then drops them every year.
quests.hint: Horns on cows and sheep never fall off, but this animal's headgear does.
quests.explanation: Deer antlers are made of bone and fall off each year, then grow back. Horns stay for life.
quests.funFact: Antlers are some of the fastest-growing tissue of any animal.
quests.question: Deer

quests.instruction: Name the wild animal with curved tusks that it uses for digging and for defending itself.
quests.hint: Its tusks are really long, sharp teeth that curl up beside its snout.
quests.explanation: Wild boars have long canine teeth that curve upward. They help with digging and with defending themselves.
quests.funFact: A boar's tusks sharpen themselves as they rub against each other.
quests.question: Wild Boar

quests.instruction: Spot the animal that pulls its claws back inside its paws while it walks, to keep them sharp.
quests.hint: It tiptoes quietly, with its tools tucked away.
quests.explanation: Most cats can pull their claws into their paws. This keeps the tips sharp for climbing and catching prey.
quests.funFact: Cats shed the outer layer of their claws, which you may find stuck to a scratching post.
quests.question: Cat

quests.instruction: Which animal's long, curved claws hook over branches so it can hang with almost no effort?
quests.hint: Its claws work like coat hangers.
quests.explanation: Sloths' long curved claws hook over branches so they can hang upside down without using much energy.
quests.funFact: Sloths are surprisingly good swimmers.
quests.question: Sloth

quests.instruction: Spot the animal that has big, furry paws that spread wide so it doesn't sink in deep snow.
quests.hint: Think of how snowshoes spread out your weight.
quests.explanation: Wolves have large paws that spread their weight and let them travel across snow.
quests.funFact: A wolf's paws have scent glands that leave a smell behind as it walks.
quests.question: Wolf

quests.instruction: Which bird uses its strong, curved beak to crack hard nuts and to help it climb?
quests.hint: It can use its beak like an extra foot.
quests.explanation: Parrots have strong, curved beaks that crack nuts and help them grip branches as they climb.
quests.funFact: A parrot's thick, muscly tongue helps it handle food and copy sounds.
quests.question: Parrot

quests.instruction: A short, thick, cone-shaped beak is just right for cracking small seeds. Which bird has one?
quests.hint: It works like a tiny nutcracker.
quests.explanation: Seed-eating birds like finches have short, strong, cone-shaped beaks. Their beak shape fits the food they eat.
quests.funFact: The finches of the Galápagos Islands have beaks of different shapes, each suited to a different food.
quests.question: Songbird

quests.instruction: Find the bird that has a pointed bill and a tongue covered in backward-facing spikes to hold slippery fish.
quests.hint: The spikes stop dinner from escaping.
quests.explanation: Penguins have backward-pointing spines in the mouth, which keep slippery fish from sliding out.
quests.funFact: Gentoo penguins are among the fastest swimming birds, at about 35 kilometres an hour.
quests.question: Penguin

quests.instruction: On a freezing morning, which animal fluffs up its feathers to trap a layer of warm air?
quests.hint: Its feathers are for flying and for keeping warm.
quests.explanation: Fluffed-up feathers trap air next to the body. That layer of air works like a cosy blanket.
quests.funFact: A small songbird can have thousands of feathers.
quests.question: Songbird

quests.instruction: Which sea animals keep warm in icy water with a thick layer of fat instead of fur?
quests.hint: The fat under its skin acts like a winter coat.
quests.explanation: Whales have a thick layer of fat called blubber. It keeps them warm and stores energy.
quests.funFact: The blubber of a bowhead whale can be about half a metre thick.
quests.question: Whale

quests.instruction: When the days get shorter, which farm animal grows a thicker coat to stay warm?
quests.hint: Its coat gets thicker before the cold sets in.
quests.explanation: Horses grow thicker winter coats as the days shorten, and shed them again when it warms up.
quests.funFact: A horse swishes its tail and mane to brush away flies.
quests.question: Horse

quests.instruction: Name the animal that chews wood to keep its front teeth from growing too long.
quests.hint: Its front teeth never stop growing.
quests.explanation: A beaver's front teeth keep growing all its life. Gnawing on wood wears them down and keeps them sharp.
quests.funFact: A beaver's lips close behind its front teeth, so it can chew underwater without swallowing water.
quests.question: Beaver

quests.instruction: Pick the reptile that has cone-shaped teeth made for gripping, not chewing.
quests.hint: Its teeth hold on tightly to slippery prey.
quests.explanation: Crocodiles have pointed teeth for gripping. They swallow big chunks rather than chewing.
quests.funFact: A crocodile has around sixty teeth, and it can replace them when they wear out.
quests.question: Crocodile

quests.instruction: Pick the animal that has flat back teeth for grinding grass and a tough pad instead of upper front teeth.
quests.hint: It grinds its food side to side, like a millstone.
quests.explanation: A cow's flat back teeth grind tough grass, and a hard pad in the upper jaw replaces the front teeth.
quests.funFact: A cow can make about a hundred litres of saliva in a day.
quests.question: Cow

quests.instruction: Which animal flicks out a long, sticky tongue, attached at the front of its mouth, to catch insects?
quests.hint: The tongue is fastened at the front, so it can flip out fast.
quests.explanation: A frog's sticky tongue is attached at the front of its mouth, which lets it flip out and snatch insects.
quests.funFact: When a frog swallows, it pulls its eyeballs down into its head to help push the food along.
quests.question: Frog

quests.instruction: Pick the animal that can use its trunk like a snorkel while it crosses a deep river.
quests.hint: It holds the tip of its nose above the surface.
quests.explanation: An elephant can swim across deep water, holding the tip of its trunk above the surface to breathe.
quests.funFact: African elephants have ears shaped a little like the continent of Africa.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Which animal's eyes seem to glow in the dark because of a mirror-like layer inside them?
quests.hint: A layer at the back of the eye bounces light back out.
quests.explanation: A cat's eye has a mirror-like layer that reflects light, which helps it see in dim light and makes its eyes shine.
quests.funFact: A cat's pupils can open wide in the dark and shrink to thin slits in bright sunlight.
quests.question: Cat

quests.instruction: Name the farm animal that uses its long, tufted tail like a fly swatter.
quests.hint: It flicks back and forth over its back all day.
quests.explanation: Cows swish their tails to chase away biting flies.
quests.funFact: The tuft of long hair at the end of a cow's tail is called the switch.
quests.question: Cow

quests.instruction: Which animal flaps its huge ears to cool itself on a hot day?
quests.hint: The ears are full of blood vessels that give off heat.
quests.explanation: An elephant's ears have lots of blood vessels. When it flaps them, the air cools the blood.
quests.funFact: An elephant can spread its ears wide to look bigger when it feels threatened.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Pick the animal that has its eyes on the sides of its head, so it can see nearly all around.
quests.hint: Eyes on the sides help spot danger coming from any direction.
quests.explanation: Rabbits have eyes on the sides of their heads, so they notice danger from nearly every direction. Hunters like lions and owls have eyes at the front, which helps them judge distance.
quests.funFact: A rabbit can see behind it without turning its head.
quests.question: Rabbit
